text: The SSA fee-agreement cap is $9,200 (lesser of 25% of past-due benefits or $9,200), effective for favorable decisions on or after November 30, 2024.

text: Under 20 CFR 404.988, an SSA Title II determination can be reopened within 12 months of the initial-determination notice for any reason, and within 4 years for good cause.
notes: LEAD ONLY - no fetched evidence (WebFetch DNS outage). Lead source IDs: GS10. Analog to VA CUE/earliest effective date but time-limited, unlike CUE which has no time limit.

text: Under 20 CFR 404.988(c), an SSA determination can be reopened at any time only for enumerated conditions such as fraud or similar fault, not for general legal error.
notes: LEAD ONLY - no fetched evidence (WebFetch DNS outage). Lead source IDs: GS10. Enumerated list also includes e.g. another claim on the same earnings record; full list not verified.

text: SSA good cause for reopening does not include a change of legal interpretation or administrative ruling (20 CFR 404.989(b), as described in Kassin, 945 F.2d 114).
notes: LEAD ONLY - no fetched evidence (WebFetch DNS outage). Lead source IDs: GS11, GS10. Weakens the 'law as it read then' angle in SSDI relative to VA CUE: there is no open-ended reopening for legal error after 4 years.

text: The SSI good-cause reopening window (20 CFR 416.1488) is 2 years rather than 4.
notes: LEAD ONLY - no fetched evidence (WebFetch DNS outage). Lead source IDs: GS10. Lead from search summary only.

text: SSDI retroactive benefits cannot reach more than 12 months before the application date and exclude a five-month waiting period from the established onset date; SSI pays only from the month after filing.
notes: LEAD ONLY - no fetched evidence (WebFetch DNS outage). Lead source IDs: GS12. Law-firm blog lead; SSR 18-01p text not retrieved. This caps the dollar value of earliest-date work per SSDI claim far below VA retro awards.

text: When a prior SSA application is reopened, SSA can use the earlier application's filing date for back-benefit eligibility; there is no dedicated form - the claimant files a new application and asks SSA to reopen.
notes: LEAD ONLY - no fetched evidence (WebFetch DNS outage). Lead source IDs: GS13. Representative-firm blog lead. Practitioner sources also say an ALJ cannot reopen another ALJ's decision.
